heard: Half of the moon is permanently frozen in total darkness, right. Pop culture calls it the dark side, but that term originally meant unexplored. In October 1959, the Soviet Luna 3 probe took the first photographs of this unseen face. Operating spacecraft on the far side requires relay satellites because the moon blocks radio signals. On January 3, 2019, China's Chang'e 4 achieved the first soft landing on the far side. Sunlight sweeps across the entire lunar surface in a repeating cycle of approximately 29.5 days. During a new moon, the far side is actually bathed in blazing daylight. Both sides share equal sun, proving that no side is permanently frozen in total darkness.
